name: token-pie
description: Local, machine-wide visibility into GitHub Copilot token and AI-credit spend.
author: Ashish Koshy

commands.title: Token Pie: Enable Local Trace Collection
Token Pie: Purge Retained Prompt Content

tokenPie.refreshIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often to poll `agent-traces.db` for new spans.

tokenPie.creditsPerNanoAiu.markdownDescription: Conversion from `copilot_usage_nano_aiu` to AI Credits. **Calibrate against your GitHub billing dashboard before trusting absolute figures.**

tokenPie.statusBar.enabled.description: Show today's spend in the status bar.

tokenPie.autoPurge.enabled.markdownDescription: After each ingest, delete the model output and tool schemas that `github.copilot.chat.otel.maxAttributeSizeChars` cannot suppress. This is the only case where Token Pie writes to Copilot's database. Measured at under 3 ms in steady state; a locked database is skipped, not waited on.

tokenPie.autoPurge.busyTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long the automatic purge waits for a database lock before giving up. Kept short so it never stalls Copilot; the purge is idempotent, so a skipped cycle is harmless.

tokenPie.rateCard.autoUpdate.markdownDescription: Once a week, fetch a newer copy of GitHub's published model prices from `tokenPie.rateCard.url`. The extension ships a dated snapshot and works offline without this; the fetch only keeps the *comparison* against your measured rates current. Set to `false` for no outbound requests.

tokenPie.rateCard.url.markdownDescription: Where the weekly refresh reads published prices from. Point this at your own file if you are on negotiated or enterprise pricing; the format is the bundled `rate-card.json`. A response that does not parse as a complete rate card is discarded rather than partly applied.

tokenPie.rateCard.models.markdownDescription: A rate card supplied inline, overriding both the bundled snapshot and any fetched copy. Same shape as `rate-card.json`. Use this to price a model GitHub does not publish, or to correct one.

tokenPie.pricing.minObservations.markdownDescription: A model shows no solved rate card, so no per-token prices and no cost split. _Three coefficients need more than three observations. Six leaves three degrees of freedom, which is the fewest that lets the R2 check below fail._

tokenPie.pricing.minR2.markdownDescription: A rate card that fits worse than this is discarded rather than shown. _Cost is an exact rate card, not a trend, so a correct fit lands on 1.000000. Anything materially below means the model is wrong -- a tier change mid-window, or a token class we do not know about. Note this guard has never been near-missed, so it is unfalsified rather than proven: it admits fits a thousand times worse than any observed._

tokenPie.advice.minHistoryRequests.markdownDescription: All recommendations are withheld below this much total history. _Five requests can be one session that went badly. Ten is where the depth buckets start to fill, so "how you work" is visible rather than inferred from a single conversation._

tokenPie.advice.minBaselineRequests.markdownDescription: A model with fewer cache-hit requests gets no cache-miss finding. _A rate needs more than one observation to be a rate._

tokenPie.report.minBucketRequests.markdownDescription: A depth bucket below this is left out of the thread-depth ratio. _A "3.6x" headline was once stated from two observations against two. This asks whether there is enough to compute a rate, not whether it matters._

tokenPie.report.minPricedShare.markdownDescription: Below this share of spend priced, the composition falls back to token counts. _A cost split covering a minority of the bill would look like the whole of it._

tokenPie.projection.minDaysForRate.markdownDescription: No burn rate, so no throttle projection -- the verdict reads "no-rate". _This was 0.5, which is exactly the one-heavy-afternoon case it exists to exclude; a test projecting a throttle from a single burst caught it._

tokenPie.advice.minCreditsAtStake.markdownDescription: A finding worth less than this is not shown as a pattern. _A floor in absolute terms, so a trivial sum cannot qualify on share alone._

tokenPie.advice.minShareAtStake.markdownDescription: A finding below this share of observed spend is not shown as a pattern. _Asks whether this is a real slice of how the person works, independently of whether it threatens the allowance._

tokenPie.advice.minShareOfAllowance.markdownDescription: A finding this large against the remaining allowance is shown as urgent, whatever its share of spend. _The urgent path exists because a finding can be small against history and still decide whether the allowance survives the period._

tokenPie.advice.minCacheFactor.markdownDescription: A cache-miss finding is withheld unless misses cost this multiple of hits. _Below this the multiple is ordinary variance rather than a finding._

tokenPie.advice.autoDominantShare.markdownDescription: Above this share, advice says Auto chose the model rather than you. _Telling someone to route away from a model Auto picked is advice about a decision they never made, so the wording has to follow who chose._

tokenPie.report.cacheWriteDominant.markdownDescription: Above this, fresh input is labelled "and cached for next time" and the surcharge is explained; below 1 minus this, "charged in full". _Between the two the population is genuinely mixed and neither wording is true, so the label says neither._

tokenPie.projection.tightDaysMargin.markdownDescription: Headroom below this reads "tight" rather than "ok". _One heavy day changes the answer at this margin._

tokenPie.reconcile.roundingSlack.markdownDescription: Absolute slack before two credit figures are called different. _quota_remaining arrives rounded to one decimal, so a delta of two readings can be off by 0.1 through rounding alone._

tokenPie.reconcile.relativeTolerance.markdownDescription: Proportional slack added to the absolute one above. _Rounding alone does not scale with the window; this absorbs the drift that does._

tokenPie.history.days.markdownDescription: How far back transcripts are read, and how long rollups are kept. _One monthly billing period plus slack. Longer costs a slower first scan._

scripts.test: tsc -p . && node scripts/entitlement.test.mjs && node scripts/projection.test.mjs && node scripts/advice.test.mjs && node scripts/confidence.test.mjs && node scripts/pricing.test.mjs && node scripts/depth.test.mjs && node scripts/fleet.test.mjs && node scripts/backfill.test.mjs && node scripts/reconcile.test.mjs && node scripts/tuning.test.mjs && node scripts/ratecard.test.mjs && node scripts/console.test.mjs && node scripts/responsive.test.mjs && node scripts/selftest.mjs
